parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The respiratory quotient (RQ) values for different respiratory substrates can be calculated.

Table 5.1 shows:

* the formulae of four respiratory substrates
* the number of oxygen molecules ($O_2$) needed to completely respire each substrate to carbon dioxide and water.

Table 5.1

| respiratory substrate | formula | number of oxygen molecules needed for respiration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *beta*-hydroxybutyric acid | $C_4H_8O_3$ | 4.5 |
| glucose | $C_6H_{12}O_6$ | 6.0 |
| malic acid | $C_4H_6O_5$ | 3.0 |
| oleic acid | $C_{18}H_{34}O_2$ | 25.5 |

Using Table 5.1, name the respiratory substrate with the highest RQ and the respiratory substrate with the lowest RQ.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
In anaerobic conditions, the production of ATP in mammals and yeast involves glycolysis and fermentation.

Describe the similarities **and** differences between fermentation in mammals and in yeast.
